errors.english: causes the mind that grasps non-existence to sever the continuity
errors.why: The cognition of non-existence (by producing a discordant cause) cuts off the continuum of the cognition of the entity; the English makes the entity-cognition the causer.

errors.english: just as coldness is produced by fire
errors.why: The example is cold being removed by fire (as cold [ceases] from fire), not cold produced by fire.

note: A difficult apoha/virodha passage rendered largely correctly; two clauses misconstrued.
Faithful rendering of the regress argument against space's nature and the six Vaiśeṣika categories.

errors.english: You should generate faith through conviction in deities
errors.why: ལྷར is an e-text slip for ལྟར ('as will come below'); the text asks for the faith of conviction, not conviction in deities.

note: Clear and accurate account of the sequence of faith and the instruction for stabilising it.

errors.english: the sign of the third is certainly established
errors.why: The phrase concedes that the triply-characterised sign is established as known; 'of the third' and 'certainly' misread it.

note: The anvaya/vyatireka argument about the word 'niścita' is followed correctly overall.

errors.why: ཕྱིར here is causal: the lemma is 'because it is experienced', glossed by 'because one experiences it functioning at that very time'.

note: Mostly follows the dream/waking argument but the prose is murky in places and one lemma is misconstrued.

errors.english: the first (Sanghadisesa) Formal Meeting of the Sangha
errors.why: This is the Mūlasarvāstivāda saṅghāvaśeṣa; the Pali form is used where the Sanskrit tradition is meant.

fix.find: the first (Sanghadisesa) Formal Meeting of the Sangha

errors.why: The term is nyes byas (Skt. duṣkṛta); 'dus-kyas' is a garbled equivalent.

note: Content of the Vinaya commentary is rendered correctly; terminology glosses need tidying.

errors.english: the Tathagata made a supremely radiant stupa
errors.why: 'Supremely illuminating' qualifies the Tathāgata, who honoured the body and also built stūpas; it is not an attribute of the stūpa.

note: The verses are understood correctly; one epithet is attached to the wrong noun.

errors.why: The objection is about the phrase sādhyasādhana, 'that which proves the probandum', as itself the qualifier, not about the probandum being established by the prover.

note: The root verses and the general-rule/exception argument are rendered well; one objection is misparsed.

errors.english: Through the pride of the lord of men
errors.why: Continuing མ་བཀུར་ from the previous side (Skt. vimānena): the king was slighted/dishonoured by this; it is not his pride.

fix.find: Through the pride of the lord of men
fix.replace: Slighted by this, the lord of men

note: The narrative and the deity's speech are rendered faithfully apart from the opening line.

errors.english: is a plural term used to express clarity
errors.why: གསལ་བ here is vyakti, the individual instances; the plural is used because the particulars are meant.

fix.find: is a plural term used to express clarity
fix.replace: is a plural term, because the individual instances (vyakti) are meant

errors.english: If a support makes the state of destruction occur through itself or another
errors.why: The hypothesis is that the support makes the perishing thing persist (stay), not that it brings about destruction.
མཚམས་སྦྱོར་བ is rebirth-linking (pratisandhi); the mental consciousness that links rebirth is the 'being'.

note: Follows the refutation of a support for persistence in outline, but several technical terms are misread.
